books.title: From Clay to Keyboard
books.subtitle: A short history of writing
books.author: Henrik Dahl
books.description: How did people first learn to store words outside their heads? This short history follows writing from counting tokens and clay tablets in Mesopotamia, through hieroglyphs, the alphabet and the scrolls of the ancient world, to monks copying books by hand, the printing press, and the screens and keyboards we write on today.

books.title: Linear Algebra, Visually
books.subtitle: Vectors, matrices and the mathematics behind modern AI
books.author: Workbench Learning
books.description: A short, beautifully illustrated introduction to linear algebra for curious adults, students and anyone heading into data science or AI. It builds real intuition before formulas: vectors as arrows and lists, length and the dot product, matrices as machines that move space, matrix multiplication, solving systems of equations, and eigenvectors. Every chapter has clear diagrams, worked examples you can check by hand, code you can run, and Check your knowledge questions.

books.title: LLMs from Zero to Expert 1: Getting Started
books.subtitle: What large language models are and how to begin
books.author: Workbench Learning
books.description: The first volume of a ten-part course that takes you from complete beginner to expert in large language models. It explains in plain words what AI, machine learning and LLMs are, how a model predicts the next token, what tokens are, how a whole answer is generated, where LLMs came from, how to write your first good prompts, what LLMs can and cannot do, and how to set up your learning workbench. Every chapter has diagrams, examples you can run, and Check your knowledge questions with answers and explanations.

contents.title: Tokens: How a Model Reads Text
From One Token to a Whole Answer
What LLMs Can and Cannot Do

books.title: Money Made Simple
books.subtitle: A first guide to budgeting and saving
books.author: Elena Marsh
books.description: A calm, practical introduction to managing everyday money. Learn where your money really goes, build a simple monthly budget, set up an emergency fund, deal with debt step by step, and make saving automatic. Written for people who find money stressful and want a plan they can actually keep.

books.title: Python in Small Steps
books.subtitle: A gentle first book on programming
books.author: Tomas Reyes
books.description: Never written a line of code? This short book takes you from "what is a program?" to writing small useful scripts of your own. Each chapter introduces one idea, shows it in a few lines of Python, and ends with a small exercise. No maths beyond adding up, and no jargon left unexplained.

books.title: Ten Quiet Minutes
books.subtitle: Simple habits for a calmer day
books.author: Samuel Adeyemi
books.description: You do not need an hour of meditation or a retreat in the mountains to feel calmer. This small book offers ten-minute practices you can fit into an ordinary busy day: a gentler morning, breathing that settles the body, walks that clear the head, a quieter relationship with your phone, and an evening routine that leads to better sleep.

contents.title: An Evening That Leads to Sleep

books.title: The Lighthouse at Gull Point
books.subtitle: A story for young readers
books.author: Mira Holloway
books.description: Ten-year-old Nell spends a summer with her grandfather, the last keeper of the lighthouse at Gull Point. When a storm knocks out the light on the night the fishing boats are due home, Nell must find the courage to climb the tower alone. A warm story about family, the sea and being brave when it matters.

contents.title: The Long Road to the Sea
